easy.explanation: Psalm 18:1 says, “I will love thee, O LORD, my strength.”
easy.q: Who does David call his strength?

easy.explanation: David calls the LORD his rock, fortress, deliverer, buckler, and high tower.
easy.q: What is the LORD called in verse 2?

easy.explanation: Psalm 18:3 says, “so shall I be saved from mine enemies.”
easy.q: From whom does David expect to be saved?

answers: David declares that the LORD is his source of strength and deliverance
David boasts in his own military power
medium.explanation: The opening combines David’s love and trust in the LORD with confidence in His protection.
medium.q: What is the main idea of the opening verses?

answers: The LORD protects and saves David in many ways
David does not know God’s name
medium.explanation: Rock, fortress, deliverer, buckler, and high tower all express safety and salvation.
medium.q: What do the many names for the LORD emphasize?

answers: The source of David’s saving strength
medium.explanation: In this context, the horn represents strength and victorious salvation.
medium.q: What does “the horn of my salvation” most nearly mean?

answers: God’s deliverance leads David to confess the LORD as his strength
Deliverance causes David to reject the LORD
challenge.explanation: After speaking of salvation, David identifies the LORD as his rock, fortress, and deliverer.
challenge.q: How are David’s deliverance and his trust connected?

answers: The LORD as a rock and fortress
The LORD as smoke and hail
The LORD as an enemy and pursuer
challenge.explanation: A rock and fortress suggest dependable protection.
challenge.q: Which image most strongly communicates stability and safety?

answers: He has moved from danger to deliverance
He has moved from joy to sorrow
He has moved from kingship to slavery
challenge.explanation: The passage introduces a song of confidence in the LORD’s saving power.
challenge.q: What change in David’s situation is implied by the opening?

easy.explanation: Psalm 18:4 says, “The sorrows of death compassed me.”
easy.q: What compassed David?

easy.explanation: Psalm 18:6 says, “In my distress I called upon the LORD.”
easy.q: Whom did David call upon in his distress?

easy.explanation: Psalm 18:5 says, “The snares of death prevented me.”
easy.q: What prevented David?

answers: As danger surrounding him on every side
medium.explanation: Sorrows of death, floods of ungodly men, and snares of death create a picture of surrounding danger.
medium.q: How is David’s distress portrayed?

medium.explanation: David cries unto God, and the passage says that God hears his voice.
medium.q: What does David do because of the danger?

medium.explanation: A snare is a trap or entangling danger.
medium.q: What does “snares” mean in “the snares of death”?

answers: It shows that danger surrounded David
It shows that the enemy disappeared
It shows that David was in an open field
challenge.explanation: To be compassed is to be surrounded or enclosed.
challenge.q: How does the word “compassed” intensify the description of distress?

answers: Sorrows of death, floods of ungodly men, and snares of death
challenge.explanation: These expressions appear in the two verses describing David’s peril.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes the danger in verses 4–5?

answers: David’s cry to God is his response to distress
David expects his enemies to save him
challenge.explanation: David calls upon the LORD when the dangers surround him.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the movement from danger to prayer?

easy.explanation: Psalm 18:7 says, “Then the earth shook and trembled.”
easy.q: What happened to the earth when the LORD appeared?

easy.explanation: The passage describes smoke, fire, darkness, hailstones, thunder, and lightning.
easy.q: Which elements appear in the description?

easy.explanation: Psalm 18:10 says, “And he rode upon a cherub, and did fly.”
easy.q: Upon what did the LORD ride?

answers: Divine power and the shaking of the world
medium.explanation: The earthquake, fire, thunder, and lightning portray the LORD’s overwhelming power.
medium.q: What do the natural phenomena communicate?

answers: With darkness, dark waters, and thick clouds
medium.explanation: The LORD makes darkness His secret place, surrounded by dark waters and thick clouds.
medium.q: How is the LORD’s hidden place described?

medium.explanation: The phrase directly refers to heavy clouds in the sky.
medium.q: What are “thick clouds of the skies”?

answers: Thunder expresses the LORD’s voice and power
Thunder is unrelated to the LORD
Thunder represents the voice of David’s enemies
challenge.explanation: Verse 13 says, “The Highest gave his voice,” in the midst of thunder and hail.
challenge.q: How is thunder connected with the LORD’s voice?

answers: The earth shakes, fire and clouds appear, then thunder and lightning follow
challenge.explanation: The description progresses from the shaking earth to storm imagery and divine weapons.
challenge.q: What is the general order of the revelation in this section?

answers: A sense of all-encompassing divine power
A limitation of the LORD’s power
A description only of David’s emotions
challenge.explanation: The many cosmic images show creation responding to the LORD’s presence.
challenge.q: What effect does the abundance of natural imagery create?

easy.explanation: Psalm 18:16 says, “He drew me out of many waters.”
easy.q: From what did the LORD draw David?

answers: His strong enemy and those who hated him
The people of his own city only
easy.explanation: Verse 17 names David’s strong enemy and those who hated him.
easy.q: From whom did the LORD deliver David?

easy.explanation: Psalm 18:19 says, “He brought me forth also into a large place.”
easy.q: Where did the LORD bring David?

medium.explanation: The waters are part of the danger from which God rescues David.
medium.q: What do the many waters symbolize in this passage?

medium.explanation: Verse 19 says, “he delivered me, because he delighted in me.”
medium.q: Why does the passage say the LORD delivered David?

medium.explanation: The wording describes God’s action in pulling David out of the waters.
medium.q: What does “he drew me out” mean in context?

answers: Many waters versus a large place
challenge.explanation: David moves from threatening waters into an open, spacious place.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in the passage?

answers: The divine power revealed in creation also acts to save David
The two passages have no connection
challenge.explanation: The powerful LORD who shakes creation also reaches down to rescue His servant.
challenge.q: How does this personal rescue continue the previous description?

answers: David faced both a powerful enemy and numerous opponents
David had only one harmless enemy
challenge.explanation: The verses emphasize both the strength of the enemy and the number of those who hated David.
challenge.q: What do the references to a strong enemy and many haters suggest?

easy.explanation: Psalm 18:21 says, “For I have kept the ways of the LORD.”
easy.q: What does David say he has kept?

easy.explanation: Psalm 18:27 says, “For thou wilt save the afflicted people.”
easy.q: What will the LORD do for the afflicted people?

easy.explanation: The same verse says, “but wilt bring down high looks.”
easy.q: What will the LORD do with high looks?

answers: His righteousness, clean hands, and obedience to the LORD
medium.explanation: David repeatedly mentions righteousness, clean hands, keeping God’s ways, and avoiding iniquity.
medium.q: On what does David base his description of reward?

answers: David says he kept God’s judgments and statutes before him
medium.explanation: David says God’s judgments were before him and that he did not put away His statutes.
medium.q: How are God’s judgments related to David’s integrity?

medium.explanation: The expression refers figuratively to proud or haughty looks.
medium.q: What do “high looks” represent?

answers: God’s response is described in relation to a person’s character and conduct
challenge.explanation: Verses 25–26 contrast the merciful, upright, pure, and froward according to their ways.
challenge.q: What principle is suggested by “With the merciful thou wilt shew thyself merciful”?

answers: The LORD gives David light and enlightens his darkness
challenge.explanation: Verse 28 says, “thou wilt light my candle” and “enlighten my darkness.”
challenge.q: How does the candle image relate to David’s deliverance?

answers: The LORD saves the afflicted and brings down the proud
The afflicted are unworthy of help
challenge.explanation: Verse 27 directly contrasts salvation for the afflicted with the bringing down of high looks.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between humility and salvation here?

paragraphs.title: Strength, Protection, and Victory in Battle

easy.explanation: Verse 32 says, “It is God that girdeth me with strength.”
easy.q: Who strengthens David?

easy.explanation: Psalm 18:34 says, “He teacheth my hands to war.”
easy.q: What does God teach David?

answers: They were pursued, wounded, and subdued
easy.explanation: The passage describes David pursuing, overtaking, wounding, and subduing his enemies.
easy.q: What happened to David’s enemies?

answers: He strengthens him, steadies his steps, and protects him
He delivers David to his enemies
medium.explanation: God gives strength, makes David’s way perfect, provides a shield, and keeps his feet from slipping.
medium.q: How does God help David in battle?

medium.explanation: Hinds are swift-footed animals, so the image suggests agility and stability.
medium.q: What does the image of feet like hinds’ feet suggest?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to those who opposed David in battle.
medium.q: What does “those that rose up against me” mean?

answers: God’s protection enables David to act and overcome his enemies
The shield prevents David from fighting
The shield belongs only to the enemies
challenge.explanation: God gives David the shield of salvation, and the following verses describe military victory.
challenge.q: How are the shield and victory connected?

answers: God-given stability enables David to advance against his enemies
challenge.explanation: After describing secure steps, David describes pursuing and overtaking his enemies.
challenge.q: What does the movement from “my feet did not slip” to pursuing enemies suggest?

answers: They called for help but received no deliverance
They received protection from the LORD
challenge.explanation: Verse 41 says they cried even unto the LORD, but He answered them not.
challenge.q: What does “They cried, but there was none to save them” reveal about David’s enemies?

answers: The strivings of the people and his enemies
easy.explanation: Verse 43 says God delivered David from the strivings of the people, and verse 48 speaks of deliverance from enemies.
easy.q: From what did God deliver David?

answers: Give thanks and sing praises to the LORD
Ask them to fight against God
easy.explanation: Verse 49 says, “Therefore will I give thanks unto thee, O LORD, among the heathen, and sing praises unto thy name.”
easy.q: What will David do among the heathen?

easy.explanation: The final verse speaks of God’s mercy to His anointed, to David, and to his seed for evermore.
easy.q: To whom does God show mercy for evermore?

answers: He moves from being threatened to being made head of the heathen
He moves from king to servant
He moves from deliverer to captive
medium.explanation: God delivers David and makes him “the head of the heathen.”
medium.q: What change in David’s status is described?

medium.explanation: Verses 44–45 say the strangers hear, obey, and submit themselves.
medium.q: How do the strangers respond when they hear of David?

medium.explanation: The strangers are pictured as fading away and being afraid out of their concealed or enclosed places.
medium.q: What does “their close places” suggest?

answers: God’s deliverance leads David to praise Him before the nations
Deliverance causes David to hide his faith
challenge.explanation: After describing God’s deliverance and exaltation, David promises thanks and praise among the heathen.
challenge.q: How are deliverance and thanksgiving connected?

answers: God changes David from one rescued from enemies into a leader with authority
The nations become David’s only protectors
challenge.explanation: God first delivers David and then makes him head of the heathen.
challenge.q: What does the movement from personal rescue to rule over nations mean?

answers: It celebrates God’s salvation, praise, kingship, and enduring mercy to David’s seed
It adds only another description of danger
challenge.explanation: The conclusion exalts the living God, thanks Him for deliverance, and affirms His everlasting mercy to David and his seed.
challenge.q: How does the ending gather together the psalm’s main ideas?
